verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The market empties out and the pigeons take the square.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone left a coin
on the ledge, still warm—
I pocket it, walk on.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The evening light thins out
where the coin's shadow lay—
I keep walking, lighter now.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A pigeon lands where the coin was—
finds nothing, doesn't mind,
lifts off with the last of the light.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The square exhales its noise—
somewhere a shutter clangs shut,
and I forget which pocket.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I check my hand anyway—
empty, warm from something,
the square already forgetting me too.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A bell somewhere counts the hour—
I stop pretending to remember,
let the dark finish the count.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The lamps take over the counting—
one by one, without hurry,
each one sure of its small circle of light.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Someone's window catches the last one—
a curtain pulled soft against morning,
already dreaming past my count.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The kettle clicks off in another room—
I was not counting that either,
just the steam finding its own way out.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Frost on the sill keeps its own tally—
no hand to wipe it clean yet,
just light, arriving slowly, to take the count.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The gate left open all night—
nobody comes to close it,
just the cold walking through, unhurried.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A dog barks twice, then thinks better of it—
the street holds its breath a moment,
settling back into what it was.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Somewhere a door forgets to latch itself—
the hinge keeps its opinion quiet,
letting the wind decide what happens next.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A kettle ticks as it cools on the stove—
no one left to pour it,
just steam finding its own way to the window.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A moth studies the lampshade like scripture—
no one home to switch it off,
so it keeps reading the same bright line.
